claims.claim: When a departing partner or contractor is converted to a Single-Channel Guest, chat-user-management.md has the admin disable 2FA and repoint the account's email to a personal address 'nobody here controls,' while the account stays live and retains full DM history access. Because sensitive-information.md lists 'email (messages)' as sensitive data and treats Slack DMs as a plausible leak surface for secrets/PII, anyone who later compromises that former user's personal mailbox can run Slack's password-reset flow (no working 2FA to stop it) and inherit standing read access to that person's entire historical DM archive, including any sensitive material shared with them while employed.

public-vulnerability-disclosure.md states HackerOne/GSA Bug Bounty is 'the only intake we publish' and that a report arriving another way (email, public channel) 'cannot be worked from where it landed' with 'no separate route' to move it in. security-incidents.md's reporting channels (itservicedesk@gsa.gov, gsa-ir@gsa.gov, Slack #incident-response) are built for TTS staff self-reporting internal incidents, not for triaging inbound public vulnerability tips, so a real external report sent to any of those addresses instead of HackerOne has no defined path into GSA SecOps' triage process, leaving a known, reported vulnerability unaddressed and exploitable for as long as the reporter is stuck outside the one working channel.

time-tracking-and-rates.md confirms that when the Tock team enters hours on an employee's behalf (e.g., for OOO periods), 'the timesheet has no field for who submitted the entry' and the weekly timekeeping check only confirms a timecard exists, not who filed it. finance-and-billing.md treats Tock-derived utilization and billable hours as the basis for charging partner agencies and for monitoring TTS financial health. Because the two mechanisms combine into an unattributed write path onto a record that directly drives client billing, hours can be added to an engagement's Tock report by someone other than the billed employee with no field or check capable of later distinguishing a legitimate proxy entry from an unauthorized one — a gap only visible by reading the billing consequences in finance-and-billing.md against the missing submitter-identity control in time-tracking-and-rates.md.

state-local-agreements.md has the account manager merely 'confirm' informally that a delegation or authorizing statute exists when an IGCA request letter is signed by someone other than the chief executive, and explicitly states 'the instrument itself is not collected' and 'is not one of the items assembled into the package that goes for review and signature.' agreements.md establishes that OGC's review is the actual control gate before an agreement is executed and funds obligated. Because the authority check happens only as an unverified AM attestation upstream of the one enforced review step, a forged or nonexistent delegation could ride through OGC review undetected — the review that is supposed to be the check happens where the missing document would never be seen.
